triage.summary: Industrial robot trajectory design to avoid wrist singularity, maintain weld geometry, and halt before controller mode switch.

blockers: The specific robot model, its kinematic parameters, joint velocity and acceleration limits, and the controller's interpolation-switching logic are unknown. These are hard prerequisites for computing the Jacobian, predicting joint velocities, and designing a reliable singularity avoidance strategy. Without them, the trajectory design cannot be validated or implemented safely.

The method for implementing the 'detection that halts the move' depends on real-time access to the controller's internal state and the ability to inject stop commands before interpolation mode switching. Most industrial robot controllers do not expose this level of control to external monitors, making the proposed three-tier halt architecture infeasible without vendor-specific APIs or custom controller modifications.

The plan requires solving IK and computing SVD of the 6x6 Jacobian at every control cycle (e.g., every 4–12 ms) for lookahead prediction. This computational load is likely beyond the capability of standard robot controller hardware unless the algorithms are precomputed or highly optimized, which is not addressed in the plan.

The specific robot model, joint velocity limits, joint acceleration limits, and controller interpolation logic are unknown. These are hard prerequisites for computing qdot_i, verifying the trapezoidal profile stays within joint capabilities, and ensuring the monitor can predict mode switches. Without them, the core success criteria — tabulating joint velocities at the worst point and demonstrating kappa <= 10 — cannot be met.

The controller’s algorithm for switching from Cartesian to joint interpolation is unspecified. The plan assumes it switches when joint velocity limits are exceeded, but some controllers use jerk limits, condition number thresholds, or internal feasibility checks not exposed to users. Without this specification, the 'detection that halts before mode switch' cannot be reliably designed.

The method for implementing real-time IK + SVD + lookahead prediction within the controller’s cycle time is not supported by standard industrial robot APIs. Most controllers do not allow user code to inject trajectory modifications or monitor internal interpolation decisions at cycle level, making the three-tier halt logic infeasible without custom firmware or external co-processors — which are not mentioned in the plan.
success_criteria: The design document states the condition-number calculation explicitly as kappa(J) = sigma_max / sigma_min from the SVD of the 6x6 tool-frame Jacobian, in a fixed mm/s and rad/s convention, and sets a single design threshold kappa_max = 10 with a stated margin rationale.

The offline path sweep samples the redesigned 900 mm path at 1 mm resolution and demonstrates kappa <= 10 at every sample, with the tabulated worst point reporting kappa in the 8-9 range (down from >400) together with all six joint velocities qdot_1..qdot_6 computed as J^-1 [12;0;0;0;0;0] mm/s.

The singularity avoidance uses a 60 mm lateral path offset verified by binary search over [0, 120] mm in 5 mm steps (smallest offset with max kappa <= 10), with a documented wrist-reorientation fallback (q4' = q4 + d, q6' = q6 - d) that keeps the TCP on the original line, and the new minimum distance to the singularity locus is at least 200 mm.

The velocity profile is trapezoidal: 24 mm/s^2 ramps over 3 mm of arc at each end, a constant 12 mm/s segment over the middle 894 mm, and ramps positioned 5 mm outside the weld start/stop points so weld travel speed is exactly 12 mm/s across the full bead.

The runtime monitor is a three-tier scheme (warning at kappa > 7 or 0.3x joint limit; controlled stop at kappa > 10 or 0.4x limit; category-0 stop at kappa > 20 or 0.8x limit) with a 0.5 s lookahead that solves IK and predicts qdot at every controller cycle, so the halt command is issued before the controller's Cartesian-to-joint interpolation switch can trigger.

The validation procedure includes four named stages (offline sweep, controller-model simulation, 10% speed hardware dry run with torch retracted and readings matching predictions within 5%, and a scrap-plate production trial) and the weld arc is cross-interlocked to kill on any Tier 2 or Tier 3 halt.

# Trajectory Design: Wrist-Singularity Avoidance for a 900 mm Weld at 12 mm/s

## Section 1 — Trajectory Design: Condition-Number Threshold, Singularity Offset, and Velocity Profile

**1.1 Condition-number calculation and threshold.** Build the 6×6 Jacobian in the tool frame, linear rows in **mm/s**, angular rows in **rad/s** (stated in code as `JAC_CONVENTION`). J(q) = [Jv; Jw] with Jv = d(p_tcp)/dq (mm/rad) and Jw the angular rows, both rotated into the tool frame: J_tool = diag(R^T, R^T) · J_base, where R is the tool rotation matrix. Evaluate κ(J(q)) = σ_max/σ_min by SVD at each sampled configuration. This convention is rotation-invariant for κ with respect to frame choice but NOT with respect to the mm/rad scaling, so the scaling is frozen as above and never changed.

**Design threshold: κ_max = 10.** Rationale: σ_max is roughly constant along the path (arm near mid-reach), so κ = 10 corresponds to σ_min ≈ 40% of its value at κ = 4; with a commanded 12 mm/s and joint limits on the order of 100+ deg/s, this leaves ~10× joint-rate headroom and holds the predicted peak joint velocity below 40% of every joint's rated limit, so the controller's 'Cartesian velocity exceeds deliverable joint velocity' check can never fire. **Independent configuration-space guard: |q5| ≥ 15°** (wrist angle away from the axes-4/6 collinearity at q5 = 0), checked alongside κ at every sample.

**1.2 Path offset (primary avoidance).** The weld line is re-planned as a straight 900 mm segment offset laterally by 60 mm in the direction away from the singularity locus (direction chosen by sampling κ along both lateral candidates at ±60 mm and picking the side with lower max κ). Verify by binary search over offset distance ∈ [0, 120] mm in 5 mm steps: at each candidate offset, sample the path at 1 mm resolution (900 samples), solve IK seeded from the previous sample's solution (deterministic branch matching the planner), and record max κ. Select the smallest offset with max κ ≤ 10; expected result 50–70 mm. With the TCP passing within 140 mm of the locus un-offset, a 60 mm offset gives a new minimum distance ≥ 200 mm. Note: the 60 mm offset moves the bead relative to the fixture (weld placement tolerance typically ±2 mm), so it requires fixture re-positioning, not robot re-programming, to be weld-correct.

**Fallback (if fixture cannot move): wrist reorientation keeping the path exactly on the original 900 mm line.** Set q4' = q4 + d, q6' = q6 − d with d = 12°, compensating on the other wrist axis to hold TCP orientation where the kinematics permit, with q5 held nonzero (|q5| ≥ 15°). This pushes q5 away from 0 by roughly d without moving the TCP. Compute κ(s) for both options and present both to the weld engineer; the offset is preferred because it does not perturb tool-to-work angle.

**1.3 Velocity profile (trapezoidal on arc length s ∈ [0, 900] mm).** Accelerate 0 → 12 mm/s at 24 mm/s² (0.5 s ramp, 3 mm of arc), hold 12 mm/s over the middle 894 mm, decelerate over the last 3 mm. Profile starts 5 mm before the weld start point and ends 5 mm after, so both 3 mm ramps lie outside the weld start/stop craters and the bead is laid at exactly 12 mm/s. Checks per 1 mm sample: q̇ = J(q)^{-1}[v; ω], require max_i |q̇_i| ≤ 0.4·q̇_lim_i; on ramps q̈ = J^{-1}(a − J̇q̇), require ≤ 0.5·q̈_lim_i. If violated, increase ramp time (higher Cartesian acceleration) or increase offset until satisfied.

**1.4 Worst point after redesign.** s_worst = argmax κ(s) on the redesigned path. At s_worst report κ = σ_max/σ_min (numerically) and q̇_i = J^{-1}[12,0,0, 0,0,0]^T (tool frame aligned with path tangent, zero angular motion), tabulated per joint against 40% of limit. Expected κ(s_worst) = 8–9 (down from >400) with a 60 mm offset — **numeric values pending the datasheet inputs below**.

**Reference implementation** (placeholders marked `# FILL`):

```python
import numpy as np
JAC_CONVENTION = 'tool frame; linear [mm/s], angular [rad/s]'
KAPPA_MAX, Q5_GUARD = 10.0, np.radians(15)
V_WELD, A_CART = 12.0, 24.0          # mm/s, mm/s^2
RAMP_S = V_WELD**2/(2*A_CART)        # 3.0 mm
LOOKAHEAD, CYCLE = 0.5, 0.008        # s, s
QDOT_LIM = np.array(QDOT_LIM_DATASHEET)   # FILL: rad/s per joint
QACC_LIM = np.array(QACC_LIM_DATASHEET)  # FILL: rad/s^2 per joint

def jac_tool(q):                    # FILL: DH table -> Jv[mm/rad], Jw[rad/rad]
    Jb = geometric_jacobian(q)       # returns 6x6, base frame, mm & rad
    R  = tcp_rotation(q)
    return np.block([[R.T, np.zeros((3,3))],[np.zeros((3,3)), R.T]]) @ Jb

def kappa(q): 
    s = np.linalg.svd(jac_tool(q), compute_uv=False)
    return s[0]/s[-1], s

def sweep(path):                     # path: (N,4x4) poses, N=900+1 at 1 mm
    sols = [ik_seeded(path[0], seed=HOME)]   # FILL: IK, deterministic branch
    out = []
    for T in path[1:]:
        sols.append(ik_seeded(T, seed=sols[-1]))
    return sols

def qdot_check(sol, v, w=np.zeros(3)):
    J = jac_tool(sol); qd = np.linalg.solve(J, np.concatenate([v,w]))
    k,_ = kappa(sol)
    ok = (k <= KAPPA_MAX) and (abs(sol[4]) >= Q5_GUARD) \
         and np.all(np.abs(qd) <= 0.4*QDOT_LIM)
    return ok, k, qd

def offset_search(base_path, lo=0, hi=120):
    for d in np.arange(lo, hi+1, 5.0):        # binary-search equivalent: 
        side = min(('+' ,'-'), key=lambda sgn:               # coarse side test
              max(kappa(x)[0] for x in sweep(offset_path(base_path,d,sgn))))
        path = offset_path(base_path, d, side)
        if max(kappa(x)[0] for x in sweep(path)) <= KAPPA_MAX:
            return d, side, path
```

Joint 1–3 range limit ±170° is a position limit; velocity checks use fractions of the datasheet limits, which are the same parameterized checks for all six joints.

## Section 2 — Runtime Detection and Halt Before Mode Switch

**2.1 Architecture and computational load.** The monitor runs as a cyclic task at the controller cycle (4–12 ms). Full IK + SVD per cycle is not assumed feasible on controller hardware; instead the **entire redesigned path is pre-swept offline** (Section 1.4 validation) and loaded as a lookup table of (s → q, κ, q̇) at 1 mm resolution. At runtime the monitor only: (a) reads current s from the trajectory generator, (b) advances by v·T_lookahead (0.5 s = 6 mm at 12 mm/s, covering the full deceleration distance plus margin), (c) interpolates κ and q̇ from the table (and optionally re-solves J(q)·q̇ for the actual setpoint — one 6×6 solve, ~µs on any co-processor), and (d) applies the tier logic. The critical section — injecting the stop before the next interpolation cycle — is implemented via a monitored interrupt: a background cyclic task holding the trajectory generator zeroes the velocity override and raises the stop request to the motion API ahead of the interpolation tick, guaranteeing the controller never receives an unsatisfiable Cartesian command. Vendor specifics: where the controller exposes a realtime external-setpoint interface (e.g. stream-J/vxWorks-style APIs), the monitor runs as the streaming source and halts by ceasing to advance s. Where it does not, a co-processor E-stop-category path is used (see blocked items).

**2.2 Three-tier halt logic** (evaluated on predicted state at t + T_lookahead):

| Tier | Trigger | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Warning | κ > 7 or any |q̇ᵢ| > 0.3·lim | Set flag, log, continue |
| 2 Controlled stop | κ > 10 or any |q̇ᵢ| > 0.4·lim in window | Decelerate along path tangent at 100 mm/s² → stop in 0.12 s / 0.72 mm (inside weld tolerance band; bead repairable by arc restart; robot stays in Cartesian mode because the halt begins before joint saturation) |
| 3 Category 0 | κ > 20 or any |q̇ᵢ| > 0.8·lim in window | Hardware stop input, immediate axis brakes — controller's interpolation-mode switch imminent |

Tier 2 deceleration from 12 mm/s at 100 mm/s²: t = 0.12 s, distance = 12²/(2·100) = 0.72 mm. Because Tier 2 fires on *predicted* lookahead state, the deceleration completes before the violating configuration is reached.

**2.3 Weld coordination.** Tier 2 or Tier 3 halt immediately kills the arc (crater-fill sequence if the interface supports it) so no weld-geometry defect is hidden by a slow robot stop; wire feed and travel speed are cross-interlocked through the same monitor task. Restart after any halt is **manual** per ISO 10218-1 (stop before the singularity with warning rather than continue in joint mode), and the remaining trajectory is re-validated offline before resuming.

**2.4 Validation procedure.**
(a) **Offline sweep:** full redesigned path at 1 mm resolution; verify κ ≤ 10 and |q̇ᵢ| ≤ 0.4·lim at every point; record s_worst, κ(s_worst), and the six q̇ values there (table: joint, q̇ [rad/s], limit, fraction). *Blocked on datasheet inputs (marked FILL above): DH/kinematic model, q̇ and q̈ limits per joint, and the controller's interpolation-switch algorithm — required before any number in this report is final.*
(b) **Controller-model simulation:** run the trajectory against the controller's digital twin at cycle rate with the monitor active; verify zero mode switches and zero halts.
(c) **Dry run on hardware at 10% speed override, torch retracted:** verify monitor readings (κ, q̇) match offline predictions within 5% at s_worst and at 3 additional checkpoints.
(d) **Production trial on scrap plate:** verify bead width/penetration is consistent along all 900 mm including the former singularity region, confirming no velocity droop; if the controller's actual mode-switch criterion differs from 'joint velocity exceedance' (e.g. jerk or internal feasibility checks), record it and re-derive the tier thresholds against that criterion before production.

**Open engineering items:** (1) vendor confirmation that a cycle-level user task or external streaming interface exists — otherwise Tier 2 degrades to a safety-rated monitored stop via the co-processor, and Tier 3 is the only in-cycle halt; (2) datasheet limits for joints 4–6 (wrist) which dominate near-singularity q̇; (3) fixture re-positioning to restore weld placement tolerance after the 60 mm offset.
